sources.entry: smart-open - Stream files from S3, GCS, Azure, HDFS, and HTTP as a drop-in replacement for open().

summary.one_liner: smart_open is a Python library that streams large files from remote storage (S3, GCS, Azure, HDFS, HTTP and more) and local disk through a drop-in replacement for the built-in open().
use_cases: stream a large S3 object line by line without downloading it
read gzip or bz2 files transparently in Python
write output directly to a cloud bucket from Python code
read files over SFTP or HTTP with the same open() call
iterate over keys in an S3 bucket in parallel
use Path.open to read compressed text files
notable: Drop-in replacement for open() with the same API across many storage backends
Transparent (de)compression inferred from file extension, with register_compressor for custom formats
transport_params and client_kwargs let you pass your own boto3, GCS or Azure clients
iter_bucket processes S3 bucket keys in parallel with multithreading
caveats: Optional dependencies are not installed by default; each backend needs its own extra
Kerberos auth needs extra packages (requests-kerberos, paramiko[gssapi]) installed separately
hdfs:// and viewfs:// shell out to the Hadoop hdfs command-line client, which must be on PATH
HTTP and HTTPS transports are read-only
